items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: The best second cornet player I ever had in my band was Alfred Lane.

ctx.x: The best second cornet player I ever had in my band was Alfred Lane. Oh, yeah. Hmm.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Alfred Laine Interview, 1951-04-21
items.q: My daddy got a band for me, and he started me out playing, so I played with my dad.

ctx.x: Well, didn't you have your own band while your daddy's was called?
Oh, yeah, and I had my band, Baby Lane. My daddy got a band for me, and he started me out playing, so I played with my dad. What instruments did you play? I played a trumpet.
Any other instruments? Well, yeah. I, yeah, yeah. I, yeah, yeah. I, yeah, yeah.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: Yeah, I got a daughter. And there's seven years difference between them, between Alfred and Alma.

ctx.x: No. I'm sorry to say, but I know. Raymond came by that very night. He was a pretty good son of a player, Johnny. Yeah, I had a boy. Swell draft player. Yeah. Swell draft player. Yeah. I'm not a player. You start to say something about your son a few minutes ago, but he never was very big or strong, really.

No, he never was, no. He didn't play all the Franks. Alfred, Alfred never was a big stride. He was always delicate, Lord. Always delicate. Always delicate. You just had one child? No, I got a daughter. Oh. Yeah, I got a daughter. And there's seven years difference between them, between Alfred and Alma. Oh. And so, Alfred, he was always sickly, all the time. But then after a long, he got a long time, and then he got diabetes, he got a stroke. And after that, he got the diabetes. And three months before he died,…
Well, I guess Abby won't take any sugar, huh? Nothing.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: Now, this is a queer thing with our boy, Alfred.

ctx.x: Yeah. You remember that one? That's old. Oh, yeah. Tell him I found a record of Kentucky Days yesterday. He found a record of Kentucky Days yesterday. Oh. Yeah.

That was my favorite. Is that right? I'll tell you a little instance that's happened about Kentucky Days. Now, this is a queer thing with our boy, Alfred. I've got three bands in Biloxi. Understand me? Uh-huh. I've got a band for West End Junior, band for West End Fire Company, number three, and a band for volunteer, number one. Okay. It was a park right on the other side of Kennedy's Hotel. Great big park. And there was a military band in this park. And there was a park. And there was a park. And they were…
